items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: a couple of my friends, Chuck Domenico and Larry Bynum who was black

ctx.x: And it’s like where are they and why don’t they have an interest in this music.

I think it’s a lot of lack of education, I really do. I don’t think they have — they haven’t taken many courses in anything like this, and — because I have black kids come and say man I never heard this kind of music. Because they’re into rap and hip hop, and it’s a faster pace and it’s — and history is a pain in the ass to most of these people. You know they take my course because it says pop. Or before it was jazz-rock foundations. And there’s a sense that these courses are — because if it’s not in their major…

so many of these kids coming to the college don’t belong in college. You know? And there’s a lot of support at Buffalo State and this was a very black dominated administration at the high end, when Muriel came in and you had to be very careful what you said. I remember Don Metz, who runs the stuff over at Birchfield, he’s an avante garde player, he’s a fabulous fabulous person, probably the best friend I have here. That’s why I do a lot of stuff with them. And he always cooked a lot of food. Great food. So…
